answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x and isolated to the primary region, which matches the March pattern where a regional traffic shift restored latency. Rollback is unavailable (security patch must stay). Circuit breaking is rejected because failing fast would drop customer writes. Read-replica routing previously helped when report/dashboard reads were loading the primary, but this incident cites heavy settlement writes, not read offload. Pre-peak headroom helped a past surge, yet that was provisioned before the window and does not explain a primary-only fault. Failover during daily settlement peak can jeopardize in-flight writes and downstream settlement completeness, so that risk is flagged and the cut should stay a controlled experiment rather than an immediate full flip. Root cause (regional infra vs release vs saturation) is still uncertain; verifying the failover record before committing is the highest-value archive pull.
